# Loose end

A loose end is an unresolved [Reference](./reference.md): the author knew *that* they were
referring to something but not *which* node it is, so the reference carries a description
of what they saw — never an ID, never a proposed name. A loose end is not a graph edge:
the index records it as a work item but must not follow the descriptor as if it named a
target.

## How it works

```text
[[?person: someone from logistics]]      unresolved — type hint + descriptor
[[?: the broker thing]]                  unresolved — type unknown
head: "?person: someone senior"          frontmatter loose end (quoted for the leading ?)
```

- A `?` immediately after the opening brackets marks the reference unresolved; everything
  after the colon is a free-text descriptor. The type after the `?` is a hint — optional,
  and overridable by the [Entity-creation pass](./entity-creation-pass.md).
- In frontmatter the same form appears bare and quoted (`?` is YAML-reserved); it lets a
  structured field name something that does not exist yet, and it is recorded as a loose
  end, *not* an edge ([Frontmatter edge](./frontmatter-edge.md)).
- Loose ends are **package-agnostic**: a descriptor is unresolved by definition, so its
  package is unknown — Vairë never guesses a package any more than it guesses an ID.
- Loose ends live **inline inside records** ([Record](./record.md)); there is no separate
  capture store, promotion queue, or third tier. The work list is derived fresh from the
  files by one scan, which makes the creation pass stateless and crash-safe: the "queue"
  is the file system.
- **Resolution is additive** — it adds an ID target and preserves the original phrasing
  as display text, so the record's words never change:

```text
[[?person: someone from logistics]]  →  [[person:logistics-contact|someone from logistics]]
```

Each resolution is its own commit; the Git diff is the audit trail of which descriptor
resolved to which ID, and who decided.

## Why

A provisional slug is still a slug: two authors guessing slugs for the same referent is
the duplicate-entity problem wearing a question mark. A descriptor has nothing to collide
with, so identity gets created exactly once, in the gated pass — the autonomous path has
no syntax for asserting an identity. The full rationale is kept in
[Unresolved references carry descriptors, never proposed IDs](../decisions/descriptors-never-slugs.md); the posture it embodies is
[Reported, never guessed](../principles/never-guess.md) and [Open to uncertainty](../principles/open-to-uncertainty.md).

## In practice

[vaire unresolved](../commands/unresolved.md) lists every loose end — record, path,
type hint (`type_guess`, `null` for the typeless form), descriptor, and line — sorted by
source path and line, defaulting to this package only (`--all-packages` widens to the
linked closure; `--type person` filters on the hint). It is the work list the
entity-creation pass consumes: descriptors are clustered type-gated, matched against
existing entities alias-and-FTS first, then resolved or turned into new entities. Before
writing a loose end, the [Authoring contract](./authoring-contract.md) says to try
[vaire suggest](../commands/suggest.md) first;
[vaire render](../commands/render.md) renders an unresolved reference as its plain
descriptor, because it is not a link.
